comment: Acceptance thresholds of the Ф1 perf gates (final-architecture.md §363-384). Keys are exact `<bench>.<metric>` names as printed by the bench scripts; values are MAXIMA. run-all.mjs --check fails when any metric exceeds its maximum — and also when a key has no matching metric, so a threshold cannot silently pass. The Ф1 'append <= 1 ms p99 (enqueue frozen entry)' budget is gated on `offthread.enqueueP99Ms`: bench-worker-commit.mjs measures the real enqueue into the storage worker, while bench-append.mjs is a legacy-path simulation (read+parse+clone+raw write, no enqueue) whose numbers (append.legacyWriteP99Ms, append.totalMsMean, append.totalLastMs, append.degradationX, append.trendMsPerIter) are informational and deliberately unthresholded. The `offthread.*` rows gate the durable path (commit work on the worker thread, Ф1 'not on the main thread'); `bridge.stallP99Ms` is the explicit stall budget under which the bridge fallback stays acceptable. The Ф2 rows: `resume.totalMs` gates 'открытие/resume ≤1 с' on the LAZY open (capsule + retained window slice, bench-open-resume.mjs), `resume.rssDeltaMb` enforces the 'RSS ≤ 500 МБ' budget on that lazy path (bench-open MATERIALIZES the corpus and is exempted by design); `prep.p95Ms` gates 'prep ≤50 мс p95' (manifest→compile at any history length), `prep.warmP95Ms` the warm goal (100% cache hits, no re-hashing; ≤5 мс on the calibration machine, ≤8 мс after the ×1.6 CI normalization below), and `prep.payloadBytes` the 'payload ≤32 МБ всегда' gate measured over the PROVIDER payload bytes (dialect-normalized wire segments from the wire compiler — the byte truth that goes to the provider, not the raw manifest). `resume-backend.totalMs` gates the same '≤1 с' budget on the REAL indexed backend path (capsule meta row + range read through sqlite-zstd, bench-open-backend.mjs) — O(window) reads, size-independent except the open consistency check. The Ф3 steering rows gate steering-design-sol.md §6.1/§6.2 on REAL clocks and the REAL sqlite-zstd backend (bench-steering.mjs, synthetic-admission corpus): `steering.enterSavedAck*` gates 'Enter → durable saved-ack p95 ≤100 мс, p99 ≤250 мс', `steering.releaseP99Ms` gates 'saved-ack → committed release p99 ≤250 мс'; the composed in-process enter→release span (steering.enterToRelease*) is informational here — the provider-request hop of §6.2 (p95 ≤500 мс) is measured by the steering e2e test in local-runtime-v2. CI normalization (approved): the four shared-runner-noise rows (`append.stallP99Ms`, `offthread.stallP99Ms`, `bridge.stallP99Ms`, `prep.warmP95Ms`) are scaled x1.6 over their local-machine calibration of 5 ms — shared macos-15 runners measurably flap them around the line on unchanged code (prep.warmP95Ms 2.98/3.66 vs 5.44/5.58 across runs; bridge.stallP99Ms 4.74 vs 9.05). Real regressions survive the normalized budget; the flapping stopped.
